# Issue Development Workflow

## Analysis
- Understand the problem statement.
- Gather and analyze requirements.
- Identify stakeholders and their needs.

## Planning
- Break down the issue into manageable tasks.
- Estimate time and resources required.
- Prioritize tasks based on importance and deadlines.

## Design Pattern Selection
- Evaluate design patterns that fit the problem:
  - Consider patterns like MVC, Singleton, or Strategy depending on the requirements.
  - Justify choice of pattern based on expected outcomes and maintainability.

## ToDo Checklist
- [ ] Complete issue analysis.
- [ ] Create an initial draft of the solution.
- [ ] Review the code with peers.
- [ ] Write corresponding tests.
- [ ] Update documentation.

## Testing Strategy
- Define testing methods:
  - **Unit Testing:** Test individual parts of the application in isolation.
  - **Integration Testing:** Test combined parts of an application to see how they work together.
  - **End-to-End Testing:** Simulate real user scenarios.
- Ensure proper code coverage (aim for at least 80%).

## PR Guidelines
- **Pull Request Title:** Clearly describe the changes made.
- **Description:** Include a summary of the changes along with any necessary context.
- **Linked Issues:** Reference any relevant issues in the PR.
- **Reviewers:** Assign reviewers who will verify the changes.
- **Labels:** Add appropriate labels (e.g., `bug`, `enhancement`, etc.).

## Conclusion
Following this workflow will improve the quality of issues resolved and maintain a consistent approach across the team.
